If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. Virtual Fly Brain holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells, including alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes. Specifically, gamma Kenyon cells are known to exist, as they innervate only the gamma lobe in the adult. According to the literature, as summarized in vfb, these subtypes can be categorized based on their axon projections to different lobes (Lee et al., 1999; Aso et al., 2014). VFB holds data on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression, with [3](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of gamma Kenyon cell") images, [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell") subclasses, [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping gamma Kenyon cell") overlapping expression patterns, [6](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for gamma Kenyon cell") scRNAseq datasets, and 23 transgene expression records available.

results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, as stated in the VFB database. results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") Kenyon cells is acetylcholine. This information comes from VFB neurotransmitter tags, which support [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") as cholinergic, i.e. using acetylcholine, as retrieved by the VFB query. results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response:
The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which states that any antennal lobe projection neuron sends synaptic output to the mushroom body, specifically the mushroom body calyx and lateral horn. 

According to the literature, as summarized by Virtual Fly Brain, antennal lobe projection neurons generally send axons to higher brain centers, including the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. 

VFB holds data on the connections of the antennal lobe, including its connections to the mushroom body and lateral horn, as well as other brain regions. 

Note that the [antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a specific type of neuron, but the provided evidence does not specifically mention its connections.

results.response: The adult Drosophila central brain contains approximately more than 125,000 neurons, according to the Virtual Fly Brain database, as retrieved from VFB. results.response:
The main components of the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge, as stated in the VFB database. These components are associated with various functions, although the specific functions are not detailed in the provided evidence. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the adult central complex, including images, neuron information, parts of the complex, tracts and nerves, lineage clones, and transgene expression data, with notable counts such as [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") neurons with some part in the adult central complex, [68](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of adult central complex") parts of the adult central complex, and [13781](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in adult central complex") images of neurons with some part in the adult central complex.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response: The dopaminergic input to [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") output neurons (MBONs) comes from various types of dopaminergic neurons. According to the VFB database, specific DAN types, including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons and adult dopaminergic PAM neurons, connect to MBONs. Additionally, dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and other PAM neurons, such as dopaminergic PAM neuron 6 and dopaminergic PAM neuron 8, also provide input to MBONs. The VFB database contains information on 77 upstream class-connectivity partners matching "dopaminergic neuron" for MBON, with top mapped pairs including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron to adult [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, with counts of [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body"), [599](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body"), and [22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") records, respectively. Furthermore, VFB has data on [dan](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBgn0039286 "Open dan in Virtual Fly Brain"), including clusters expressing dan and fly stocks for dan, with counts of [28](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBgn0039286,expressionCluster "Run in VFB: Clusters expressing dan") and [13](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBgn0039286,FindStocks "Run in VFB: Find fly stocks for dan") records, respectively.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron, according to the VFB database. Its cell body is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind (Wu et al., 2016). LPLC2 has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer (Klapoetke et al., 2017). This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli (Klapoetke et al., 2017). LPLC2 is involved in detecting looming stimuli and eliciting a jump escape response. It connects to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. VFB holds information on over 14,000 neurons, including LPLC2, which has the ID VFB_jrch0fva.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?
results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult Drosophila is more elaborated than in larval Drosophila. According to VFB, the adult antennal lobe has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas the larval antennal lobe has around 22 glomeruli. This information comes from the VFB database, specifically from the comparison of region organization. In contrast to the adult, the larval antennal lobe is less complex, with fewer glomeruli. The [antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of neuron, but VFB does not provide specific information on how the organisation of this neuron type compares between adult and larval Drosophila. VFB holds data on various aspects of Drosophila neuroscience, including the structure and development of the antennal lobe, with 50 glomeruli in the adult and 22 in the larval stage.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
The pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn involves intermediate neuron types, specifically antennal lobe projection neurons, as stated in the VFB-supported high-level pathway: olfactory receptor neurons -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn (VFB). The antennal lobe projection neurons act as interneurons, connecting the olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. 

VFB holds a significant amount of data related to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"), including images, neurons with various types of connections, tracts/nerves, lineage clones, and transgene expression data. For example, there are [1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") neurons with some part in the adult lateral horn, and [42](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating adult lateral horn") tracts/nerves innervating the adult lateral horn. Additionally, VFB contains [1935](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult lateral horn") records of transgene expression in the adult lateral horn. 

Regarding the specific connection to the [adult lateral horn Leucokinin neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn Leucokinin neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), the available data does not provide direct information on this pathway. However, VFB's extensive collection of neuron and connection data for the adult lateral horn can be explored further to understand the neural circuitry involved. 

The information on the pathway and intermediate neuron types comes from the VFB database, while the details on the adult lateral horn and its connections are based on the available VFB data.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is as follows: 
antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. 
This information comes from the VFB database, specifically from the trace containment chain query (VFB). 
VFB holds data on neurons and images related to antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, [911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, and [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") transgene expressions in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1.

Overall, the giant fiber neuron is a well-studied neuron with a range of available data and resources, including images, transgene expression records, connectivity classes, and characterized driver lines.
